title: Beyond Completion Time: A Multimodal Approach to Characterizing Eye-Hand Coordination During the Nine-Hole Peg Test in Multiple Sclerosis

problem.summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease associated with motor, sensory, cognitive, and visual deficits that can impair upper extremity function.
statements: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease associated with motor, sensory, cognitive, and visual deficits that can impair upper extremity function.

Although the Nine-Hole Peg Test (9-HPT) is widely used to assess fine motor dexterity in MS, conventional scoring captures only overall completion time, providing limited insight into the eye-hand coordination processes underlying performance.
This study characterized eye-hand coordination during peg placement using simultaneous eye tracking, markerless hand tracking, and object detection.

limitations.summary: In this exploratory cohort, PwMS had longer completion times, with the largest increase in the return from the seated peg to the grasp of the next peg with both hands, a significant increase in object manipulation with the dominant hand, and a smaller increase in object transport that was significant only with the non-dominant hand.
items: In this exploratory cohort, PwMS had longer completion times, with the largest increase in the return from the seated peg to the grasp of the next peg with both hands, a significant increase in object manipulation with the dominant hand, and a smaller increase in object transport that was significant only with the non-dominant hand.

Manipulation durations were significantly longer in PwMS with the dominant hand and numerically longer with the non-dominant hand; transport duration was significantly longer only with the non-dominant hand.
However, because the closest fixation was identified within the interval ending at peg insertion, longer placement times provide a longer observation window.
